variants.cost: N exact subgradient calls, N exact prox solves, plus dual accumulation and averaging. Objective values need not be requested separately for this update. To evaluate delta_N in (15), additionally query g_N and solve a linear maximization over Q_R(z); this is separately charged and not a stopping requirement.
variants.name: Algorithm 1 with unit weights and constant gain
variants.output: bar_x_N=(x_0+...+x_N)/(N+1) in Q_R(z); N=0 gives z.
public_inputs: norm, Q and evaluable prox d
variants.query_and_update: For i=0,...,N-1 obtain g_i in partial f(x_i); s_{i+1}=s_i+g_i; x_{i+1}=argmin_{x in Q,||x-z||<=R}{<s_{i+1},x-z>+beta d((x-z)/R)}. This is pi_zR,beta(-s_{i+1}) in (11).
variants.requirements: Finite-dimensional normed E; nonempty closed convex Q; exact bounded objective subgradients as in Assumption 1; unit-ball prox d continuous, mu_d-strongly convex, 0=d(0)<=d<=A_d; exact prox minimization over each intersection Q_R(z). Uniform convexity uses source (2).
variants.state_and_initialization: x_0=z, s_0=0 in E*. Set gamma=LR/sqrt(2mu_d A_d) and beta=gamma sqrt(N+1)>0.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use lambda_i=1 and the same beta at every update; stop after N updates. The general positive-weight/nondecreasing-gain scheme on pp.7-8 is source context, not an extra performance variant.

variants.cost: sum_k N_k exact subgradient calls and sum_k N_k exact localized prox solves to generate y_m under the output indexing. Computing every stage's gap certificate adds at most m endpoint subgradient calls and m linear maximizations. Stage resets and radius/prox changes are separate computation. No claim that a prox solve is one first-order Oracle call.
variants.implementation_details_ref: p.9 Algorithm 2 and footnote; pp.23-24 B.3
variants.name: Algorithm 2 with known uniform convexity parameters
variants.output: y_m, the last stage's arithmetic mean, in Q. This is not the last inner iterate and not an average across stages.
public_inputs: R_0>0 with ||x_0-x*||<=R_0 for global minimizer x* of f over Q
variants.query_and_update: For k=1,...,m let R_k^rho=2^(-k)R_0^rho and N_k=floor_strict(2^(tau*k)*4L^2 A_d/(mu_f^2 mu_d R_0^(2(rho-1)))). Reset one-stage center to y_{k-1}, radius R_{k-1}, primal x_0^(k)=y_{k-1}, dual s_0^(k)=0. Run the one-stage rule for N_k updates with gamma_k=L R_{k-1}/sqrt(2mu_d A_d), beta^(k)=gamma_k sqrt(N_k+1); y_k is that stage's arithmetic mean.
variants.requirements: Finite-dimensional normed E; nonempty closed convex Q; exact bounded objective subgradients as in Assumption 1; unit-ball prox d continuous, mu_d-strongly convex, 0=d(0)<=d<=A_d; exact prox minimization over each intersection Q_R(z). Uniform convexity uses source (2). Also assume f has global minimizer x*, known initial radius containment, and known L,mu_f,rho,R_0. The epsilon restriction defines the nontrivial m>=1 branch only.
variants.state_and_initialization: y_0=x_0. Define floor_strict(t)=greatest integer strictly smaller than t. Set tau=2(rho-1)/rho and m=floor_strict(log2(mu_f R_0^rho/epsilon))+1.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Stop after m stages; no observed gap-based stopping is required. Strict integer convention applies to both m and N_k. Larger epsilon, R_0=0, unknown parameters and adaptive variants are not specified by this extracted branch.
